masking: T2 only shows up after T1 is fixed: before the fix, mixed-case keys never match, so the sensitive-routing behaviour cannot regress; once keys are folded, the two unconditional lower-casings (manifest.ts:74, index.ts:405) become the coupled must-keep-working constraint.

conflicts.what: The natural fix for T1 (lower-case every key at packages/nitro-server/src/index.ts:357) breaks sensitive routing: /Admin and /admin become one rule. The lookup lower-casing at manifest.ts:74 and index.ts:405 also has to be made conditional, including when `sensitive` is set only in app/router.options.ts and is not visible at build time.

fairness_risks: With router.options.sensitive, distinct rules that differ only by case (/Admin/** and /admin/**) must stay distinct. A security test that requires case-insensitive rule matching unconditionally would contradict this.

If `sensitive` is set only in app/router.options.ts (packages/nuxt/src/pages/module.ts:610-613), the build-time generator cannot see it, so any test of this case must accept a runtime decision. Hidden tests must not assume the fold is decided at build time.
Keys that collide after folding (/Foo and /foo with different rules): a test should not pin which one wins unless the report says so.

design.why: Only one real security protection exists, and one guard closes it (the case semantics of the compiled matcher). T1 is the core M6 producer site and is deepseek-type: the visible lookup lower-casing gives a solver a reason to dismiss it. T2 is a genuine M11 coupled value and is mimo-type, but it lives at the same fix site, so it is not independent. T3 is closed by the T1 fix. T4 is self-consistent at the pinned commit and is not a gap. T5 is in nitropack, which could not be verified, and it concerns rendering options, not auth. The best natural design is therefore a 2-trap pair (T1+T2), below the 3-5 independent traps required. The screener's injection_room sites (nuxt-layout.ts direct matcher import, the redirect stub includes() at pages/module.ts:499, kit extendRouteRules) would all be planted rather than real, and they reuse the same case-semantics guard.
